title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Food & Agriculture
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: FBI seizes the Chinese state-sponsored platforms that scanned critical infrastructure and relayed attacks through hijacked devices
items.content_text: The Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorised seizures on 26 August of QScan and QTRouter, two linked platforms run by a PRC state-sponsored group the government calls QTFY and tied to a Nanjing contractor. QScan performed reconnaissance against US critical infrastructure; QTRouter relayed the resulting intrusions through compromised routers and IoT devices so traffic arrived from ordinary domestic addresses. Both platforms are now inoperable because the seized domains were hard-coded into the malware. Named victims are federal, and the activity runs back to at least 2018. For food and agriculture the relay design is the transferable point: processing plants, cold stores and farms are full of cheap connected devices nobody patches, and that is the population these platforms recruited.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: US Department of Justice press release and unsealed court documents — corroborated by TechCrunch and UPI
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Seizures announced and confirmed 26 Aug 2026; described activity dates from at least 2018 to 2026

items.title: Food and beverage ransomware volume is climbing, and production stoppages are the recurring outcome
items.content_text: Sector analysis published in early August tracks a continued rise in ransomware against food and beverage companies, with production stoppage rather than data theft as the characteristic consequence. The reference point remains the Fairlife incident of 16 July 2026, in which the Coca-Cola-owned dairy business suspended US production after an attack compromised systems supporting manufacturing. The pattern is consistent across the sector: attackers reach the business systems that schedule, batch, label and ship, and the line stops because it cannot run without them — not because anyone manipulated a controller. Perishability then converts an IT outage into product loss within hours rather than days.
tags: Incident — Sector ransomware trend with production stoppages

items.title: A CEVA Logistics breach reached European warehouses and rippled out through the companies it serves
items.content_text: CEVA Logistics disclosed a breach affecting European warehouse operations, with customer data spilling out through the retailers and brands it serves; reporting places the intrusion between late July and early August. Third-party logistics is where a food business’s despatch data lives — what is moving, to whom, at what temperature and on what schedule. For a processor or grower the exposure is indirect but practical: an attacker holding that data has an effective basis for social engineering against your despatch desk, your carriers and your customers, and warehouse disruption at a 3PL is a cold-chain problem long before it is a data-protection one.
tags: Incident — Logistics breach with downstream exposure

items.title: Treasury sanctions an Iranian intelligence-directed hacking network operating inside US critical infrastructure
items.content_text: The US Treasury designated an Iranian Ministry of Intelligence and Security-directed hacking network on 24 August as part of a wider action covering nearly 60 Iran-linked people, entities and vessels, with a related State Department reward notice. Treasury states the network has breached and exfiltrated data from US energy companies, defence contractors, healthcare providers, IT firms and banks since at least late 2023. Food and agriculture is not named. What transfers is tradecraft rather than targeting: harvesting credentials, exploiting supplier footholds and collecting network documentation works the same way against a processing plant, and food businesses typically carry a long list of integrators and equipment suppliers with standing access.
tags: Incident — Nation-state targeting of US critical infrastructure

items.title: NCSC issues an alert: increased targeting of OT across multiple sectors globally, and it has already caused real-world disruption
items.content_text: The NCSC published a formal alert on 27 August stating it has seen increased targeting of operational technology across multiple sectors globally, including in the UK, by a range of threat actors, and that the activity has caused some limited real-world disruption. No victims, actors or techniques are named. Food and agriculture is not called out, but the exposure pattern is the sector’s to a fault. The NCSC’s instruction — do not assume your OT is unreachable from the internet without verifying it, because exposure arises through misconfiguration, legacy connections and unmanaged assets — describes the packaging line an OEM supports over its own 4G router, the refrigeration and CIP controllers commissioned by a contractor, the grain elevator and cold-store telemetry on a cellular link, and the plant acquired with a business and never brought under a standard build. Advisory AA26-231A already names food and agriculture among the sectors where S7 controllers are being read.
tags: Threat Intelligence — National agency alert on OT targeting

_otthreatfeed.category: Threat Intelligence — National agency alert on OT targeting

items.title: A ransomware affiliate ran an AI coding agent inside victim networks — and the exposed server shows exactly how
items.content_text: CloudSEK published analysis on 27 August of a misconfigured server belonging to a Russian-speaking Aurora ransomware affiliate, exposing tooling, command history, credential material and the operator’s Cursor chat transcripts. The campaign ran from April to July 2026 across nine countries; the operator reached domain-level or interactive access at 17 organisations, and four appeared on Aurora’s leak site. Food, agriculture, manufacturing and professional-services organisations were among those affected, which puts this page’s audience squarely in the targeting set. The notable detail is not that AI was used but where: the transcripts show the assistant helping plan Active Directory escalation and intrusion steps, compressing the time between initial access and domain control. For a processor the useful question is whether the domain account your IT team uses every day can also authenticate to the MES, the batch server or a line HMI, because this operator reached victims through domain privilege rather than any control-system exploit.
tags: Threat Intel — Ransomware tradecraft, AI-assisted intrusion

_otthreatfeed.category: Threat Intel — Ransomware tradecraft, AI-assisted intrusion

items.title: Refrigeration controllers can be switched off while the temperature display keeps reading normal
items.content_text: Claroty’s Team82 published research into commercial refrigeration controllers, with corresponding advisories from Danfoss and Copeland. The finding that matters to a food business is not remote access in itself but the divergence between what the controller does and what the operator sees: cooling can be disabled or setpoints altered while the display continues to report a normal temperature. That is a food-safety failure mode dressed as a security finding. Every HACCP monitoring assumption you hold rests on the reading being true, and a compromised controller breaks the assumption silently — there is no alarm, because the system reporting the alarm is the system that was changed.
tags: Threat intel — Refrigeration controller research with vendor advisories

items.title: Dragos counts 70 food and beverage ransomware incidents in a single quarter
items.content_text: Dragos recorded 1,140 ransomware incidents at industrial organisations in Q2 2026, up around 12 percent on Q1, with 70 of them in food and beverage. The analysis is direct about mechanism: attackers did not need control-system access to disrupt production. Encrypting ERP, MES, labelling, warehouse management and scheduling stops a line as effectively as touching a PLC and takes far less skill. For food businesses the compounding factor is time. A manufacturer of durable goods loses schedule; a food processor loses product, and the recovery clock is set by shelf life and by the regulatory records that have to accompany whatever was in progress.

items.title: CISA’s red team took a domain undetected — the tooling was fine, the monitoring was not
items.content_text: CISA advisory AA26-237A publishes paired red-team results from two critical-infrastructure organisations assessed with comparable tradecraft. One detected and responded; the other never noticed a domain compromise. The advisory is unusually direct that the difference was not product spend — both had capable tooling, but only one reviewed the output, correlated identity events and had practised the response. Food manufacturers will recognise the shape: plant systems and corporate IT commonly share one Active Directory, monitoring is frequently outsourced to a small provider, and the production estate is often excluded from detection because the alerts were judged too noisy.
tags: Threat intel — Federal red-team assessment findings

items.title: Three more exploited flaws land in KEV — a Linux kernel bug, a JFrog Artifactory path traversal and a two-year-old ownCloud authentication bypass
items.content_text: CISA added three more actively exploited flaws to the KEV catalogue on 27 August, a day after the six-flaw batch containing NetScaler. None is an ICS product, and in food and beverage that is exactly how production stops: Fairlife’s July shutdown and the wider ransomware pattern the Food and Ag-ISAC tracks both start in enterprise IT. CVE-2026-53362 is a Linux kernel flaw, and the MES and warehouse-management server, historian, vision system, label printer controller and OT network sensor in most plants are Linux underneath — usually vendor appliances patched on the supplier’s timetable. CVE-2026-66384 is a path traversal in JFrog Artifactory, relevant where firmware or automation packages destined for line equipment are staged. CVE-2023-49105 is an ownCloud authentication bypass patched since late 2023; instances still exposed are typically unowned.
tags: Advisory — Three additions to the CISA KEV catalogue

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Three additions to the CISA KEV catalogue
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue addition, corroborated by Security Affairs and SecurityWeek
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Added to KEV 27 Aug 2026; ownCloud flaw originally disclosed Nov 2023

items.title: A seven-year-old SQL Server flaw is now confirmed exploited — and it is the database under your historian
items.content_text: CISA added six vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 26 August, and the one that matters most on the plant floor is CVE-2019-1068, a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft SQL Server patched in July 2019 and only now confirmed as exploited in the wild. Successful exploitation runs code under the SQL Server Database Engine service account; where that account is over-privileged — which is common on systems installed by an integrator years ago — the attacker moves off the database and onto the Windows host. In a processing plant this is the database under the MES, the batch and recipe store, the traceability and lot-genealogy system, and the food-safety records you would produce in a recall — often SQL Server instances a line integrator installed and left at the build they shipped with, on the same flat network as the HMIs. No public write-up of the in-the-wild technique has appeared, so detection guidance is thin; the federal remediation deadline is 29 August. Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-8452 was added in the same batch.
tags: Advisory — Actively exploited, CISA KEV, historian and MES databases

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Actively exploited, CISA KEV, historian and MES databases

items.title: The NetScaler flaw is now confirmed exploited and in KEV — federal deadline 29 August
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-8452 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 26 August, moving the Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway issue from a patching recommendation to confirmed exploitation in the wild. It is a heap overflow in SAML single sign-on parsing, rated CVSS 8.8, requiring no authentication, and reachable when the appliance is configured as a Gateway or AAA virtual server. Canada’s Cyber Centre reported indications of exploitation from around 17 August after a public proof of concept. In food manufacturing NetScaler commonly fronts the remote access used by plant engineers, out-of-hours support and the OEMs who dial in to fillers, packaging lines and refrigeration.
tags: Advisory — Actively exploited, CISA KEV, remote access

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Actively exploited, CISA KEV, remote access
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue addition of 26 Aug 2026 and Citrix security bulletin CTX696939 — corroborated by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and watchTowr Labs analysis

items.title: Two unauthenticated flaws in Veeam ONE 13 — the monitoring layer that watches the backups you would restore from
items.content_text: Veeam disclosed vulnerabilities in Veeam ONE 13 in knowledge-base articles published on 25 August. CVE-2026-64633 is rated CVSS v4.0 10.0 and allows remote, unauthenticated code execution on the Veeam ONE agent host; CVE-2026-65641 is rated 9.3 and lets a remote unauthenticated attacker coerce SMB authentication out of the Veeam ONE service account, which is the first step in relaying that account somewhere more useful. Veeam ONE 13.x is affected and the 12.x line is not. In food and beverage Veeam ONE typically watches backups of the MES, the recipe and batch servers and the engineering workstations — the recovery capability that decides whether a ransomware event costs a shift or a production week, in a sector where just-in-time delivery leaves no slack. There is no report of exploitation yet, but backup and monitoring servers are a standing target precisely because compromising them removes the recovery option before the ransomware runs.
tags: Advisory — Backup and monitoring infrastructure, unauthenticated

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Backup and monitoring infrastructure, unauthenticated
_otthreatfeed.source_name: Veeam knowledge-base articles KB4905 and KB4892 — corroborated by CyberScoop and Cybersecurity News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Vendor advisory published 25 Aug 2026; patched builds available the same day

items.title: A Git server exploit in KEV — and it is often where recipe and line configuration lives
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-60004 to the KEV catalogue on 25 August after reports of active exploitation. Rated CVSS 9.8, the flaw lets anyone with ordinary repository write access plant an executable Git hook and run shell commands as the Gitea service account. Gitea 1.27.1 fixed it on 27 July, so exploitation followed within a month. Self-hosted Gitea appears in food plants more often than people expect, stood up by controls engineering to hold PLC projects, HMI screens, recipe parameter sets and integration scripts. A low-privilege contractor account then becomes code execution on the machine holding your line configuration. Federal remediation was due 28 August.
tags: Advisory — Actively exploited, CISA KEV, engineering toolchain

items.title: CVSS 10.0 on a Siemens edge gateway that is dual-homed by design
items.content_text: Siemens’ August advisory set includes a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices, allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute code with elevated privileges. Ten Siemens advisories arrived in the same batch alongside Schneider Electric and Phoenix Contact publications. The relevance in a food plant is placement rather than score. Edge gateways are installed specifically to move line data out to an OEE platform, a corporate historian or a supplier cloud service, which makes them dual-homed by design and frequently the one device with a route between the production network and everything else.
tags: Advisory — Maximum severity, Siemens edge gateway

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Maximum severity, Siemens edge gateway

items.title: Fire-alarm management software stores its credentials in cleartext in memory, CISA warns
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-232-01, republishing Johnson Controls advisory JCI-PSA-2026-28, covers a flaw in Simplex Incident Manager fire-alarm management software that stores credentials in cleartext in memory, where a local attacker or malicious process could recover them. It is not a remote code execution finding, but it sits in a life-safety system, and in a food plant fire-alarm management usually shares a network and often a server estate with access control, refrigeration monitoring and building services. Recovered credentials from one of those systems are typically valid across several of them.
tags: Advisory — Cleartext credentials in fire-alarm management software

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Cleartext credentials in fire-alarm management software
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-232-01; Johnson Controls product security advisory JCI-PSA-2026-28

items.title: No login required and no patch coming — the Ebyte gateway advisory is a replacement decision
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-237-06 covers the Ebyte NE2-D11 serial-to-Ethernet gateway, whose web management interface does not consistently enforce authentication before granting administrative functionality. An unauthenticated remote attacker can read configuration, change settings, hijack sessions or disrupt operation. CISA notes the vendor acknowledged the reports, said a patch was in development, then stopped responding. Cheap serial converters of this class are everywhere in food and agriculture: behind older scales and checkweighers, batch controllers, grain moisture meters, bin monitors, milk tank sensors and cold-store loggers — installed because something legacy needed a network drop.
tags: Advisory — Serial-to-Ethernet gateway, no vendor patch

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Published 25 Aug 2026; re-verified 27 Aug 2026 — no vendor patch announced

items.title: From 11 September 2026 exploited vulnerabilities in digital products must be reported within 24 hours
items.content_text: The EU Cyber Resilience Act’s reporting obligations begin on 11 September 2026. Manufacturers of products with digital elements placed on the EU market must notify an actively exploited vulnerability in their product, or a severe incident affecting its security, within 24 hours of becoming aware, with fuller reporting to follow. Food and agriculture businesses are mostly buyers here, and that is the useful angle: the suppliers of fillers, packaging lines, refrigeration controllers, weighing systems and ag-IoT platforms sold into Europe acquire a defined notification duty that can be written into support contracts.
tags: Policy — EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligation

_otthreatfeed.category: Policy — EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligation
_otthreatfeed.source_name: European Commission guidance on Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations (Regulation 2024/2847)
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Regulation entered into force 10 Dec 2024; reporting obligations apply from 11 Sep 2026; full application 11 Dec 2027; status verified 27 Aug 2026

items.title: The NSA is putting an ISA/IEC 62443 certificate in front of the controllers it buys
items.content_text: ISASecure announced a partnership with the National Security Agency to develop a High Criticality Component Security Assurance certification scheme, derived from its Component Security Assurance programme and grounded in ISA/IEC 62443-4-2. Once accepted, the NSA intends to use it when adding OT components to the National Security Systems product compliant list. Food producers are not the target market, but the mechanism matters: a large buyer making certification a purchase condition changes what vendors build, and the language migrates into other specifications. For a business writing a filler, packaging or refrigeration tender, that is a citable standard rather than an invented requirement.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: ISA / ISASecure press release — corroborated by Automation World and ISSSource
